values.note: Gas-pycnometer absolute (grain) density. The sentence labels the sample 'EAC-1' but the next sentence attributes it to EAC-1A: 'As the results have shown, JSC-1A and EAC-1A have the highest bulk and absolute densities among the measured samples.' values.quote: The grain sizes in EAC-1A span from 14.6 ϕ (clay fraction) to −1 ϕ (very coarse sand), with a median value of 6.47 ϕ (~11 µm).
values.note: Approximate value ('~11 µm'), laser diffraction (Beckman Coulter LS 13 320). CONFLICT: NEW1 p.2 measured the as-received EAC-1A at 'D(v,0.1) = 22 µm, D(v,0.5) = 210 µm and D(v,0.9) = 535 µm' — an order of magnitude larger; batch/method differences, curator should be aware.

No opened document states a d50 of 181 µm for EAC-1A. R018 p.2 gives median ~11 µm (6.47 ϕ); NEW1 p.2 gives D(v,0.5) = 210 µm as received (and 694 / 282 / 49 µm for the >500, 100-500 and <100 µm sieve fractions). The only '~180' in R018 is not a d50: 'EAC-1A has a slightly lower weight percent of particles between ~180 µm and 70 µm than the lower limit of the bulk Apollo lunar regolith samples'. Also checked Zemeny 2024, Gasteiner 2026, Roth 2025, Slabic 2024, Manick 2018, Denevi 2020, LSIC 2022/2024 assessments, Duri 2022, Flahaut 2023: none pairs EAC-1A with 181. Recommend deleting or replacing with a sourced PSD string.

values.note: 2020 is the publication year of the characterisation paper (header 'Scientific Reports | (2020) 10:5473'); no document states a release date. The material predates the paper: R018 p.6 'Currently, EAC-1A is already taken in use for small-scale, low-TRL experiments undertaken by ESA', and it cites 2019 uses of EAC-1 (refs 36-37). Manick et al. 2018 (papers/Manick_etal_2018_LPSC49_abstract_1411…) lists 'EAC-1 Basanite ESA04-A 17DE01, 17DE02, 17DE03' batches at the ESA curation facility — for EAC-1, not EAC-1A. Curator may prefer 2018/2019 as first availability.

values.quote: Recently, the European Astronaut Center (EAC) in Germany, has developed EAC-1A which is a mare regolith simulant for use in the European Lunar Exploration Laboratory (LUNA) as a large-quantity material available for lunar research9.
values.note: Categorical label; wording in sources is 'available for lunar research' (NEW1) and 'EAC-1A was selected as lunar regolith simulant due to its availability in large quantities' (NEW2 p.2). R018 p.6: 'The material is also stored and curated by the ESA Sample Analogue Curation facility at ECSAT, UK38.' No formal ESA availability statement was found.

'Low-Ti' is stated by no opened document. Sources say 'mare': NEW1 p.1 'EAC-1A which is a mare regolith simulant'; NEW3 p.6 'both EAC-1A and JSC-2A being mare regolith samples'. R018 p.4 compares it to Apollo 17: 'EAC-1A is most similar to the intermediate compositions of the Apollo 17 samples30,31' and gives 'EAC-1 contains 11.9 wt% MgO and 2.4 wt% TiO2 (Fig. 3)'. Apollo 17 mare soils are the high-Ti type, so 'Low-Ti' conflicts with the stated analogue even though the simulant's own TiO2 is low. Suggest 'Mare (Apollo 17-like)' or plain 'Mare'.

results.notes: (1) R018 and R098 are the same paper (identical DOI 10.1038/s41598-020-62312-4); merge them and set local_path to papers/Engelschion_etal_2020_EAC-1A_novel_large-volume_lunar_regolith_simulant_SciRep_10-5473.pdf (two further byte-identical copies under papers/LRS/). (2) EXACT-PRODUCT CAVEAT: Engelschiøn 2020 labels grain-size-independent results (XRF chemistry, XRD, thin sections, DSC, absolute density) 'EAC-1' = the Königswinter basanite host material, and only grain-size-dependent physical tests 'EAC-1A' (p.1: 'For non-grainsize dependent tests where samples of the Königswinter basanite rock specimens have been used, these are simply labelled as EAC-1. This does not refer to a specific grain size, but to the material itself.'). The R018 oxide values in new_values therefore carry an 'EAC-1' label in the source; a curator must decide whether host-rock chemistry may be stored for EAC-1A. NEW1 values are measured directly on as-received EAC-1A. (3) NEW2's Al2O3 12.6 / Fe2O3 12 / CaO 10.8 are attributed to Engelschiøn et al. but do NOT appear in the Engelschiøn text or figure captions I read (only SiO2, MgO, TiO2, Na2O+K2O are printed; Figs 3-5 are scatter/ternary plots without tables) — treat as second-hand until the original source of those three numbers is found. (4) bulk_density: the stored 1.95 is a cohesion-test density; the paper's bulk density is 1.45 g/cm3; NEW3 reports 1.72 g/cm3 at atmospheric pressure. Zemeny et al. 2024 (papers/Zemeny_etal_2024_Luna_Analog_Facility_testbeds_EAC-1_FrontSpaceTech_1510635.pdf) reports loose/tapped bulk densities 1.46-1.99 g/cm3 and dry unit weights 1.5-2.2 g/cm3, but for 'EAC-1' (the coarse LUNA testbed material) — a different product; it names EAC-1A only in its bibliography, so it was not added as a reference. (5) d50: R018 ~11 µm vs NEW1 210 µm as received — order-of-magnitude disagreement between sources; 'd50=181' has no source. (6) Glass: R018 and NEW1 find fully crystalline; Schleppi et al. 2021 (J. Mater. Sci. 56, 12132, not in library) found ~14.4% glass per NEW1 Table 1. (7) 'Low-Ti Mare' is not stated anywhere; sources say 'mare' and 'comparable to Apollo 17'. (8) R018 abstract lists 'static angle of repose' among tests but no angle-of-repose value appears anywhere in the paper text; angle_of_repose cannot be sourced from it. (9) Other EAC-1A values seen but with no matching column: water content ~0.8 wt% (R018 p.2), 1.21% Karl-Fischer (NEW1 p.3), 1.2% (NEW2 p.7), ~1% mass loss on drying (NEW3 p.10); sphericity 0.601 / 0.591 for the 0.2-0.5 / 0.5-1 mm EAC-1 fractions (R018 p.3); melting endotherm ~1160 °C (NEW1 p.4); relative permittivity ε′ = 3.61 at 9.375 GHz at 1.72 g/cm3 (NEW3 p.8). NEW1 also reports the mineral abundances of Schleppi et al. for EAC-1A (plagioclase+K-feldspar 27.2, pyroxenes 35.5, forsterite 13.3, mica/alteration 7.6, oxides 2.0, glass 14.4 %) and NEW2 repeats Engelschiøn's thin-section modal estimate '55% plagioclase, 25% olivine and 10% pyroxene' as EAC-1A. (10) The Figueira 2022 thesis names EAC-1A but contains no simulant property data. (11) The group lists 8 of 29 library documents naming EAC-1A; I additionally checked 10 likely candidates (Zemeny 2024, Gasteiner 2026, Roth 2025, Slabic 2024, Manick 2018, Denevi 2020, LSIC 2022 and 2024 assessments, Duri 2022, Flahaut 2023): none names EAC-1A in its body text. No files were modified and nothing was fetched from the web.

(2) The extractor's library coverage was incomplete: a full-text sweep of every PDF <25 MB under Sources/papers for 'EAC-1A' found four further documents naming the exact product that the extractor never opened and that matter: Zou et al. 2024 (NEW6, 'low-Ti mare simulant EAC-1A'), Patzwald et al. 2025 (NEW7, 'general-use low-Ti mare simulant', naming 'EAC-1 or EAC-1 A'), Kjøniksen et al. 2021 ESA ACT report (NEW8, full 8-oxide EAC-1A composition in Table 1 with uncertainties, method unstated, values far from Engelschiøn's) and the arXiv v2 of Gasteiner et al. 2026 (NEW9, original EAC-1A direct-shear data, graphical only; numbers in IAC-25-A3-IP-151-97770, not in library). Because of NEW6/NEW7 the 'Low-Ti Mare' unsupported verdict is refuted, with the caveat that both are secondary statements.
